summary.overview: Freight tracks parcels that other companies carry. A Python FastAPI service answers dispatchers' status queries from a managed Redis cache, falling back to a PostgreSQL shipments database. A Node.js poller, on a timer, asks the carrier network for new scans, writes them to PostgreSQL and refreshes the Redis entry. A shared TypeScript library supplies the poller's HTTP and cache helpers. There is no UI.
findings: The API and the poller write different shapes under the same Redis key `shipment:{reference}`: the API stores a shipment row (reference, carrier, state, updated_at; `api/freight/tracking/service.py:47`), the poller stores a ShipmentScan (reference, state, scannedAt; `shared/src/cache.ts:11`). After a poll, API reads return the scan shape without carrier or updated_at.

The poller imports `@freight/shared/http`, `/cache` and `/events` (`worker/src/poller.ts:1`, `worker/src/carriers.ts:1`), but shared/package.json only sets `main` and has no `exports` map (`shared/package.json:7`), so those subpaths may not resolve; only index.ts re-exports events and http, not cache (`shared/src/index.ts:1-2`). Not verified by a build.
The poll loop has no error handling (`worker/src/poller.ts:25-28`): one failed carrier call or database error ends the process. postJson throws on any non-2xx (`shared/src/http.ts:11-13`).
The poller writes PostgreSQL then Redis with no transaction (`worker/src/poller.ts:15-17`); a failure between them leaves the cache stale for up to the 120 s TTL.

TTL_SECONDS = 120 is duplicated in `api/freight/storage/cache.py:7` and `shared/src/cache.ts:5`, and the key format is duplicated across a Python and a TypeScript implementation with no shared contract.

The shipments schema is not in the repository (no migrations), yet both services run SQL against columns they do not agree on: the poller uses checked_at (`worker/src/shipments.ts:18`), the API uses due_at (`api/freight/tracking/service.py:28`).
`worker/src/poller.ts:31` calls `await main()` at import time, so pollOnce cannot be imported for testing without starting the loop.
From the automated checks: no cycles, no unresolved references, no orphan projects; Redis and the carrier network are not compose services (CACHE_URL and CARRIER_API_URL point at .example hosts).
recommendations: Agree one cache payload shape and key format (finding 1), ideally defined once and covered by a contract test across the Python and TypeScript sides.
Add an exports map to shared/package.json, or import only from the package root, and build the worker to confirm resolution (finding 2).
Wrap each poll iteration in try/catch with logging and back-off so the poller survives a carrier outage (finding 3).
Check the shipments schema into the repo so the two services' column assumptions can be reviewed together (finding 6).
